newsitem.title: DENMARK: CSFB recommends Danish mortgage bonds.
newsitem.headline: CSFB recommends Danish mortgage bonds.

text.p: Credit Suisse First Boston investment bank recommended Danish mortgage bonds in its latest Global Strategy & Relative Value report received by Reuters on Thursday.

"Danish mortgage bonds are an obvious alternative to investors with core holdings in Danish government bonds, providing a higher direct return (100+ basis points) but with similar patterns of volatility and identical currency risk," CSFB said.

"The fact that historical experience suggests a de facto (if not pro forma) government guarantee supports the argument that these bonds are close substitutes to Danish government bonds from a risk perspective," it added.

CSFB recommended buying the Danish benchmark six percent mortgage bond due 2026 and selling the benchmark eight percent state bond due 2006 as it forecast a narrowing of the spread between the two bond series from today's approximate 105 basis points to 75-80 points.

It foresaw that as foreign investors entered Danish mortgage bonds, the supply and demand balance would improve markedly because until recently they had not been active in the segment since the mid-1980s.

CSFB said that lately foreign holdings in Danish mortgage bonds had increased from close on zero to five percent and were expected to rise to 15 percent within the next two years, with the spread narrowing accordingly.
"With EMU (European economic and monetary union) approaching, we could have a sudden jump in international interest for the segment as investors scramble to find new European markets," CSFB said.
"Global investors with an active, forward looking strategy should look into this possibility," it advised.
Denmark qualifies for participation in EMU but opted out of participation in a single European currency in a 1993 referendum and any change of stance would have to be put to fresh plebiscite.
Foreign investors held around 35 percent of all Danish state paper in 1996, purchasing a net 8.8 billion crowns worth of Danish mortgage bonds in the first quarter of 1997, central bank data shows.
